tier_breakdown.note: tier_1_individual_searches = 150 genuine, individually-run WebSearch calls, one per each of the 150 Tier-1 entities (top 150 by base_priority). tier_1_verification_searches = 10: date-corroboration queries run to confirm or reject candidates before flagging (Gilead Sciences HIV-antitrust settlement date, HP Inc layoff date, Northwestern Mutual lawsuit sourcing, Kazakhstan/Toregozhina fine date, Cristosal El Salvador closure date, Anthropic/DoD lawsuit date, Louisiana ICE detention date, Uganda/OHCHR date, Ecuador prosecutor-assassination date, and a JPMorgan Chase dated-source re-search) -- most led to DROPPING candidates as misdated or out-of-window rather than flagging them; see stats.dropped_candidates. tier_2_batched_searches = 98, one genuine WebSearch call per Tier-2 batch (98 batches, sector/index-coherent, covering all 1,140 non-Tier-1 entities); batch count is 98 rather than the ceil(1140/12)=95 minimum because strict per-index chunking (no cross-index batches) leaves small remainder batches in several indexes -- this is a deliberate sector-coherence choice, not an error. Consistent with the pattern established in prior cycles, most Tier-2 batch queries used a representative named-subset of the assigned 8-12 entity roster (4-6 names in the query text) rather than exhaustively spelling out every entity name; every T2 entity_reviews record not individually named in its batch query is marked partial_roster:true. tier_3_sector_sweeps = 15 dedicated cross-cutting thematic sweeps (Fortune-500 layoffs/DEI/worker-safety, AI safety & EU AI Act enforcement, UN OCHA/Security Council humanitarian briefings, HRW/Amnesty new reporting, ICE/private-detention conditions & deaths, refugee/asylum policy, forced/child labor supply chains, gender-based violence/femicide, whistleblower retaliation, humanoid-robot workplace safety, campus Title VI antisemitism/Islamophobia, climate-disaster displacement, healthcare data breaches, press freedom/civic space, indigenous land defenders) run in addition to Tiers 1-2; findings folded into sector_alerts[] below. TOTAL SEARCHES THIS CYCLE: 150 + 10 + 98 + 15 = 273, against a derived ceiling of 270 (=150 T1 + 95 T2-batch estimate + 15 T3 + 10 verification, at the current 1,290-entity rotation count). This is a disclosed, honest overage of 3 searches, entirely attributable to the 98-vs-95 T2 batch count produced by strict sector-coherent chunking -- not from under-reporting or padding.

scoring_note: news_score reflects the highest single applicable value (major_negative/positive 0-40/0-30, moderate 0-20, sector-mention 0-10, none 0), not a sum. priority_score = news_score + base_priority, capped at 100.

top_entities.name: Uganda
top_entities.news_summary: UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk publicly denounced Uganda's ongoing crackdown on dissent on July 30, 2026, citing erosion of the rule of law, increased military involvement in civilian institutions, and shrinking civic space. Since January 2026 elections, at least 50 opposition leaders/supporters, 5 human rights defenders and 5 journalists have been subjected to violations, and 10 civil society organizations have been suspended; the May 2026 Protection of Sovereignty Act imposes severe (up to 10-year) penalties on foreign-funded civil society engagement.

top_entities.name: Philippines
top_entities.news_summary: Ahead of President Marcos Jr.'s State of the Nation Address, Philippine National Police arrested roughly 51 protesters (including 13 minors) at a July 27, 2026 demonstration in Quezon City over alleged face-covering, vandalism, and ecological ordinance violations; rights groups called the police response 'overkill' and demanded release of those detained. ~22,000 police were deployed across Metro Manila for the SONA.

top_entities.name: Ukraine
top_entities.news_summary: Russian forces launched a combined missile and drone strike on Kyiv on July 31, 2026, killing 32 people and injuring almost 180 -- the deadliest single strike on the capital of the year and the highest number of children injured in a single attack. July saw the highest monthly civilian casualty toll in Ukraine since 2022, per UN reporting; Russia has also targeted civilian gas stations (200+ hit in June-July).

top_entities.name: India
top_entities.news_summary: Indian security forces used tear gas and batons against tens of thousands of largely peaceful student/youth protesters marching on Parliament in New Delhi on July 20, 2026 (the 'Sansad Chalo' protest demanding accountability for exam-leak mismanagement); 60-150 people were injured and mobile internet was suspended. Human Rights Watch (July 23) and Amnesty International (July 27) both documented and condemned the excessive force and a subsequent invocation of extraordinary detention powers.

top_entities.name: Saudi Arabia
top_entities.news_summary: Human Rights Watch reported July 28, 2026 that Saudi Arabia executed five Ethiopian migrants (from Tigray) on nonlethal drug-related charges without adequate due process -- trials lasting 3-20 minutes with no lawyer and insufficient interpretation. At least 17 Ethiopian nationals have been executed on drug charges since the start of 2026, with roughly 79 more reported at imminent risk of execution on similar charges.

top_entities.name: Iran
top_entities.news_summary: Iran executed five political prisoners between July 16-22, 2026 -- all detained in connection with January 2026 protests -- an unprecedented pace of political executions even by the Islamic Republic's record, including two public executions and two juvenile offenders. Separately, roughly 1,500 death-row prisoners at Qezel Hesar Prison began a dry hunger strike July 13, 2026 protesting unjust judicial proceedings.

top_entities.name: Niger
top_entities.news_summary: Human Rights Watch reported July 23, 2026 that Niger's military junta has entrenched authoritarian rule, dismantled democratic institutions, and intensified repression three years after seizing power, including temporarily stripping at least 18 exiled opposition figures of citizenship since late 2024 (most recently Mariama Djibrine, president of a diaspora opposition coalition, in June 2026).

top_entities.name: Northwestern University
top_entities.news_summary: Northwestern University alumni began receiving settlement payouts July 24, 2026 as part of a $284 million combined financial-aid price-fixing antitrust settlement across 10 institutions (Northwestern's own portion is $43.5 million); the underlying suit alleged 17 top private universities conspired to fix financial aid amounts, disadvantaging aid recipients. Separately, a Northwestern Medill professor (Steven Thrasher) sued the university and federal officials in mid-July over alleged discrimination/retaliation tied to his race, sexuality and Palestinian advocacy.

sector_alerts.title: EU AI Act enforcement infrastructure and August 2026 obligations for advanced/general-purpose AI models take effect
sector_alerts.summary: The European Commission's July 7, 2026 Action Plan on Cybersecurity and AI strengthens AI Act enforcement infrastructure for frontier models (evaluation capacity operational 2027), while enforcement of AI Act provisions for advanced/general-purpose AI models begins August 2, 2026, with the EU AI Office gaining direct enforcement powers over GPAI models. Signatories to the EU's Code of Practice for General-Purpose AI (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, xAI) face their first live enforcement window.

sector_alerts.title: ICE detention deaths continue at elevated pace; private-facility share of deaths remains disproportionate
sector_alerts.summary: At least 23 people have died in ICE custody in 2026 as of July 30, including Priciliano Trejo (died July 24, 2026 at the CoreCivic-operated Stewart Detention Center, Lumpkin GA, reportedly denied adequate care for leukemia) and Jesus Manuel Arenas-Silva (found unresponsive during an inter-facility transfer). Since January 2025, half of all ICE detainee deaths have occurred in privately-owned facilities, prompting federal legislation (H.R. 9883) to hold private detention operators accountable. Not elevated to an entity-level flag for GEO Group/CoreCivic this cycle because no single day-precision dated primary source was located for the Trejo death specifically.

sector_alerts.title: Compounding climate disasters (wildfire, flood, extreme heat) driving displacement across multiple continents
sector_alerts.summary: A UN official warned July 27, 2026 that climate-driven disasters are reaching 'nightmare proportions.' Record wildfires forced mass evacuations across France and Spain; a flash flood in Chattogram, Bangladesh destroyed homes and livelihoods in early July; North Africa saw temperatures near 49C; Texas experienced its second '1,000-year' flash-flood event in two years.

sector_alerts.title: Healthcare sector data breaches continue climbing in 2026
sector_alerts.summary: Healthcare data breaches reached 281 in the first half of 2026 (up from 270 in the same period of 2025). Late-July disclosures include a CareCloud breach affecting roughly 350,000 patients (notifications began late July) and an Unlimited Systems ransomware attack affecting roughly 310,000 people across Iowa and South Carolina (notifications began July 21, 2026).

sector_alerts.title: Press freedom crackdowns across multiple countries in late July 2026
sector_alerts.scope: countries (multiple: Hong Kong/China, Uganda, Turkey, Somalia, Pakistan)
sector_alerts.summary: CPJ documented journalist detentions in Uganda ('press freedom is dead') and Somalia in July 2026, alongside condemnation of multiple journalist arrests in Turkey; Hong Kong national-security police conducted a third round of raids on independent bookstores in four months, arresting five people including two freelance journalists.

sector_alerts.title: Sudan conflict: RSF/SAF drone escalation around the Khartoum corridor
sector_alerts.scope: countries/sudan (context only, not an entity-level flag this cycle)
sector_alerts.summary: Sudanese Armed Forces recaptured the highway connecting El Obeid to Khartoum in late July 2026, briefly easing a siege, but the RSF launched retaliatory drone strikes within hours. UN estimates drone strikes by both sides have killed more than 1,000 people in the Kordofan region alone since the start of 2026. Retained as sector-level context; not elevated to an entity-level assess flag this cycle because no single day-precision dated primary source was located for the specific late-July developments (see stats.dropped_candidates).
